value.zh: 後果復寇邊。
value.en: Later, as expected, he raided the border again.
value.literal: Later, as expected, he again raided the border.

value.zh: 轉澄鎮北大將軍、定州刺史。
value.en: Cheng was transferred to Grand General Who Guards the North and Inspector of Dingzhou.
value.literal: Cheng was transferred to Grand General Who Guards the North and Inspector of Dingzhou.

value.zh: 初，民中每有橫調，百姓煩苦，前後牧守，未能蠲除，澄多所省減，民以忻賴。
value.en: The people had long suffered from arbitrary levies, which previous governors and administrators had failed to abolish. Cheng reduced many of them, and the people rejoiced and relied on him.
value.literal: At first, whenever there were arbitrary levies among the people, the common people were troubled and suffering. The governors and administrators before and after him had not been able to remove them, but Cheng reduced many of them, and the people joyfully relied on him.

value.zh: 又明黜陟賞罰之法，表減公園之地，以給無業貧口，禁造布絹不任衣者。
value.en: He also clarified rules for promotion, demotion, reward, and punishment; memorialized to reduce public parkland and give it to poor households without livelihoods; and banned the production of cloth and silk unfit for clothing.
value.literal: He also clarified the laws of demotion and promotion, reward and punishment, memorialized to reduce the land of public parks in order to give it to poor households without occupations, and prohibited the making of cloth and silk not fit for clothing.

value.zh: 母孟太妃薨，居喪毀瘠，當世稱之。
value.en: When his mother, Grand Consort Meng, died, he wasted away in mourning, and his contemporaries praised him for it.
value.literal: When his mother, Grand Consort Meng, died, his mourning left him wasted and thin, and the age praised him.

value.zh: 服闋，除太子太保。
value.en: After the mourning period ended, he was appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
value.literal: When the mourning period was complete, he was appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

value.zh: 於時高肇當朝，猜忌賢戚。
value.en: At that time Gao Zhao controlled the court and was suspicious of worthy imperial relatives.
value.literal: At that time Gao Zhao controlled the court and was suspicious and jealous of worthy imperial relatives.

value.zh: 澄為肇間構，常恐不全，乃終日昏飲，以示荒敗。
value.en: Cheng was slandered and isolated by Gao Zhao and constantly feared for his life, so he drank heavily all day to appear ruined and useless.
value.literal: Cheng was estranged and framed by Zhao, and constantly feared he would not be preserved; he therefore drank muddily all day to show ruin and failure.

value.zh: 所作詭越，時謂為狂。
value.en: His strange, excessive behavior was taken at the time for madness.
value.literal: The strange and excessive things he did were called madness at the time.

value.zh: 世宗夜崩，時事倉卒，高肇擁兵於外，肅宗沖幼，朝野不安。
value.en: When Shizong died at night, events were sudden and confused. Gao Zhao held troops outside, Suzong was still a child, and both court and countryside were uneasy.
value.literal: Shizong died at night, events were urgent and confused, Gao Zhao held troops outside, Suzong was young, and court and countryside were unsettled.

value.zh: 澄疏斥不預機要，而朝望所屬，領軍于忠、侍中崔光等奏澄為尚書令，於是眾心忻服。
value.en: Cheng had been kept at a distance and excluded from confidential affairs, but the court's hopes rested on him. Yu Zhong, Commander of the Guards, Cui Guang, Palace Attendant, and others memorialized that Cheng be made Director of the Department of State Affairs, and everyone gladly accepted this.
value.literal: Cheng had been distantly rejected and did not take part in the essentials of policy, yet the hopes of the court rested on him. Commander of the Guards Yu Zhong, Palace Attendant Cui Guang, and others memorialized that Cheng be made Director of the Department of State Affairs, and at this the hearts of the multitude joyfully submitted.

value.zh: 又加散騎常侍、驃騎大將軍，尋遷司空，加侍中，俄詔領尚書令。
value.en: He was also made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand General of Agile Cavalry; soon he was promoted to Minister of Works with the added title Palace Attendant, and shortly afterward was ordered to concurrently direct the Department of State Affairs.
value.literal: He was also made Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand General of Agile Cavalry; soon he was transferred to Minister of Works and given the added title Palace Attendant, and shortly afterward an edict had him concurrently direct the Department of State Affairs.

value.zh: 初，正始之末，詔百司普昇一級，而執事者不達旨意，刺史、守、令限而不及。
value.en: Earlier, at the end of the Zhengshi era, an edict raised all offices by one grade, but the officials implementing it misunderstood the intent, so inspectors, governors, and magistrates were excluded.
value.literal: Earlier, at the end of the Zhengshi era, an edict had raised all the offices by one grade, but those handling the matter did not understand the intent, so inspectors, governors, and magistrates were limited and did not receive it.

value.zh: 澄奏曰：「竊惟雲構鬱起，澤及百司，企春望榮，內外同慶。
value.en: Cheng memorialized, "I humbly think that when imperial favor rose like gathering clouds and reached the hundred offices, officials inside and outside the court looked toward renewed honor and rejoiced together.
value.literal: Cheng memorialized, "I privately consider that the cloud-built grace rose richly and its favor reached the hundred offices; looking toward spring and hoping for glory, inner and outer officials celebrated together.

value.zh: 至於賞陟，不及守宰，爾來十年，冤訟不絕。
value.en: Yet the promotion did not reach governors and magistrates, and for ten years grievances and appeals have continued without end.
value.literal: But when it came to rewarding advancement, it did not reach governors and magistrates, and for ten years since then grievances and lawsuits have not ceased.

value.zh: 封回自鎮遠、安州入為太尉長史，元匡自征虜、恒州入作宗卿，二人遷授，並在先詔。
value.en: Feng Hui came in from Zhenyuan General and Anzhou to serve as Chief Clerk to the Grand Commandant, while Yuan Kuang came in from Zhenglu General and Hengzhou to serve as Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan. Both appointments occurred before the earlier edict.
value.literal: Feng Hui entered from General Who Guards Afar and Anzhou to become Chief Clerk to the Grand Commandant; Yuan Kuang entered from General Who Conquers Caitiffs and Hengzhou to become Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan. The promotions and appointments of these two men were both before the earlier edict.

value.zh: 應蒙之理，備在於斯。
value.en: These cases fully show the principle by which they should receive the benefit.
value.literal: The principle that they should receive the benefit is fully present in these cases.

value.zh: 兼州佐停私之徒，陪臣郡丞之例，尚蒙天澤下降，榮及當時。
value.en: Moreover, provincial assistants, private retainers who had ceased service, subordinate officers, and commandery deputies all received the court's favor and shared in the honor at the time.
value.literal: In addition, provincial assistants, those who had suspended private service, subordinate ministers, and commandery deputies still received the descent of heavenly favor, and the honor reached them at the time.

value.zh: 然參佐之來，皆因府主，今府主不霑，佐官獨預，棄本賞末，愚謂未允。
value.en: But assistants come forward through their chiefs. For the chiefs to receive nothing while their subordinates alone benefit abandons the root and rewards the branch; in my foolish view this is not just.
value.literal: Yet assistants come in all because of their office heads. Now the office heads do not receive the favor, while assistant officials alone participate; abandoning the root and rewarding the branch, in my foolish opinion, is not fair.

value.zh: 今計刺史、守、宰之官，請準回匡，悉同汎限，上允初旨百司之章，下覆訟者元元之心。」
value.en: I therefore ask that inspectors, governors, and magistrates be treated according to the precedents of Feng Hui and Yuan Kuang and included within the general scope, above fulfilling the original edict's words about the hundred offices, and below satisfying the hearts of the people who have appealed."
value.literal: Now, calculating the offices of inspectors, governors, and magistrates, I request that they be modeled on Hui and Kuang and all be included within the general limit, above fulfilling the original edict's phrase "the hundred offices," and below answering the hearts of the common people who have appealed."

value.zh: 詔曰：「自今已後，內外之事，嘗經先朝者，不得重聞。」
value.en: The edict said, "From now on, internal and external matters already handled under the former reign may not be reported again."
value.literal: The edict said, "From now on, matters inside and outside the court that once passed through the former reign may not be reported again."

value.zh: 澄奏曰：「臣聞堯懸諫諍之鼓，舜置誹謗之木，皆所以廣耳目於芻蕘，達四聰於天下。
value.en: Cheng memorialized, "I have heard that Yao hung up the remonstrance drum and Shun set up the criticism post, both to widen their hearing and sight among even the humblest people and let the ruler's fourfold hearing reach all under Heaven.
value.literal: Cheng memorialized, "I have heard that Yao hung the drum for remonstrance and Shun set up the wood for criticism; both were means to broaden ears and eyes among woodcutters and herdsmen and make the fourfold hearing reach all under Heaven.

value.zh: 伏惟太祖開基，化隆自遠，累聖相承，於今九帝。
value.en: Taizu founded the dynasty and his transforming rule spread far. Sage rulers have succeeded one another, down to the ninth emperor today.
value.literal: I bow and consider that Taizu opened the foundation and his transformation flourished from afar; successive sages have inherited one another, now reaching nine emperors.

value.zh: 重光疊照，汚隆必同，與奪隨時，道無恒體。
value.en: Their radiance has shone one after another; whether in decline or flourishing, the principle is the same. Granting and withholding follow the times, and the Way has no fixed form.
value.literal: Repeated radiance and layered illumination, decline and flourishing must all be the same; granting and taking follow the time, and the Way has no constant form.

value.zh: 思過如渴，言重千金，故稱無諱之朝，邁蹤三、五。
value.en: They thirsted for reflection on their faults and valued speech at a thousand pieces of gold; thus ours was called a court without taboos, surpassing the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors.
value.literal: They thirsted to think on faults and valued words at a thousand in gold; therefore ours was called a court without taboos, surpassing the tracks of the Three and Five.

value.zh: 高祖沖年纂曆，文明協統，變官易律，未為違典。
value.en: Gaozu inherited the throne while young, and Empress Wenming assisted the government. They changed offices and laws, yet did not violate classical norms.
value.literal: Gaozu succeeded to the calendar at a tender age, and Wenming cooperated in rule; they changed offices and altered laws, but this did not violate the classics.

value.zh: 及慈聖臨朝，母儀宇縣，爰發慈令，垂心滯獄，深枉者仰日月於九泉，微屈者希曲照於盆下。
value.en: When the Compassionate Sage held court, her maternal example covered the realm. She issued merciful orders and attended to stalled cases, so the deeply wronged looked up to sun and moon even from the Nine Springs, and the slightly aggrieved hoped for a slant of light beneath the overturned basin.
value.literal: When the Compassionate Sage held court, her maternal model covered the realm; she then issued compassionate orders and set her heart on delayed lawsuits, so those deeply wronged looked up to the sun and moon from the Nine Springs, and those slightly aggrieved hoped for a bent light beneath the overturned basin.

value.zh: 今乃格以先朝，限以一例，斯誠奉遵之本心，實乖元元之至望。
value.en: Now to block such cases as belonging to the former reign and limit them by one rule may be meant as obedience, but it truly violates the people's deepest hopes.
value.literal: Now to bar them by saying "the former reign" and limit them by a single rule truly follows the root intention of obedience, but in fact goes against the utmost hopes of the common people.

value.zh: 在于謙挹，有乖舊典。
value.en: As a matter of humble receptiveness, it also departs from the old institutions.
value.literal: In humility and yielding, it departs from the old institutions.

value.zh: 謹尋抱枉求直，或經累朝。
value.en: I have examined those who carry grievances and seek justice; some cases have lasted through several reigns.
value.literal: I have carefully examined those who hold grievances and seek straightening; some have passed through several reigns.

value.zh: 毫釐之差，正之宜速；
value.en: A difference of a hair's breadth should be corrected quickly;
value.literal: A difference of a hair or a li should be corrected quickly;

value.zh: 謬若千里，駟馬弗追。
value.en: if an error becomes a thousand li, even a four-horse team cannot catch it.
value.literal: if the error is like a thousand li, even a team of four horses cannot catch it.

value.zh: 故禮有損益，事有可否，父有諍子，君有諫臣，琴瑟不調，理宜改作。
value.en: Thus ritual can be reduced or augmented, affairs can be approved or rejected, fathers have sons who argue with them, and rulers have ministers who remonstrate. If zithers and lutes are out of tune, they should be adjusted.
value.literal: Therefore ritual has diminutions and additions, affairs have what may and may not be done, fathers have sons who contest them, and rulers have ministers who remonstrate with them. If zithers and lutes are not in tune, principle says they should be adjusted.

value.zh: 是以防川之論，小決則通；
value.en: Thus, in the argument over blocking rivers, a small opening lets them flow;
value.literal: Thus in the argument about blocking rivers, a small opening lets them flow;

value.zh: 鄉校之言，擁則敗國。
value.en: and as for speech in the village schools, blocking it ruins the state.
value.literal: as for speech in the village schools, if it is blocked, it ruins the state.

value.zh: 矧伊陳屈，而可抑以先朝。
value.en: How much more when people are presenting grievances: how can they be suppressed merely because they concern a former reign?
value.literal: How much more when they are setting forth grievances: how can they be suppressed by saying "the former reign"?

value.zh: 且先朝屈者，非故屈之，或有司愛憎，或執事濁僻，空文致法，以誤視聽。
value.en: Those wronged under the former reign were not wronged deliberately by the throne. Sometimes officials were moved by favoritism or hatred, sometimes clerks were corrupt and biased, and empty paperwork produced legal judgments that misled the court.
value.literal: Moreover, those wronged under the former reign were not intentionally wronged. Sometimes there was love or hatred by the offices, sometimes murky partiality among those handling matters, and empty documents brought about law, thereby misleading hearing and sight.

value.zh: 如此冤塞，彌在可哀。
value.en: Such obstructed grievances are all the more pitiful.
value.literal: Such blocked grievances are all the more worthy of pity.

value.zh: 僭之與濫，寧失不經，乞收今旨，還依前詔。」
value.en: If there is risk of excess, I would rather err on the side of irregular openness. I beg that the present order be withdrawn and that we return to the previous edict."
value.literal: As for overstepping and excess, I would rather err on the side of irregularity; I beg that the present order be withdrawn and that we return to following the previous edict."

value.zh: 詔曰：「省奏，深體毗贊之情，三皇異軌，五代殊風，一時之制，何必詮改。
value.en: The edict said, "I have reviewed the memorial and deeply understand your wish to assist the throne. The Three Sovereigns followed different paths and the Five Ages different customs; why must the institutions of one period all be revised?
value.literal: The edict said, "I have reviewed the memorial and deeply understand the feeling of assisting and supporting. The Three Sovereigns had different tracks and the Five Ages different customs; why must the institutions of one time all be weighed and changed?

value.zh: 必謂虛文設旨，理在可申者，何容不同來執。
value.en: If one says that formal texts merely express an intention and that the principle may be extended, then how could similar cases not all come forward to be taken up?
value.literal: If it is necessarily said that empty texts set forth intentions and that the principle lies in what can be extended, how could we allow them not all to come and be taken up alike?

value.zh: 可依往制。」
value.en: Let the former system be followed."
value.literal: It may follow the former system."

value.zh: 澄表上皇誥宗制并訓詁各一卷，意欲皇太后覽之，思勸戒之益。
value.en: Cheng submitted one fascicle each of Imperial Admonitions, Clan Regulations, and Explanatory Glosses, hoping the Empress Dowager would read them and consider their value for admonition.
value.literal: Cheng submitted one fascicle each of Imperial Admonitions, Clan Regulations, and Explanatory Glosses, intending that the Empress Dowager read them and consider their benefit for exhortation and warning.

value.zh: 又奏利國濟民所宜振舉者十條。
value.en: He also submitted ten recommendations for measures that should be revived to benefit the state and aid the people.
value.literal: He also memorialized ten articles on what should be revived and promoted to benefit the state and aid the people.

value.zh: 一曰律度量衡，公私不同，所宜一之。
value.en: First: statutes, measures, weights, and balances differ between public and private use and should be unified.
value.literal: The first said: laws, measures, weights, and balances differ between public and private use; they should be unified.

value.zh: 二曰宜興學校，以明黜陟之法。
value.en: Second: schools should be promoted to clarify the rules for demotion and promotion.
value.literal: The second said: schools should be promoted in order to clarify the law of demotion and promotion.

value.zh: 三曰宜興滅繼絕，各舉所知。
value.en: Third: fallen lines should be revived and extinct lines continued, with each official recommending those he knows.
value.literal: The third said: what has perished should be revived and extinct lines continued, and each should recommend those he knows.

value.zh: 四曰五調之外，一不煩民，任民之力，不過三日。
value.en: Fourth: beyond the five regular levies, the people should not be burdened, and labor service should not exceed three days.
value.literal: The fourth said: beyond the five levies, the people should not be troubled at all, and use of the people's labor should not exceed three days.

value.zh: 五曰臨民之官，皆須黜陟，以旌賞罰。
value.en: Fifth: officials who govern the people must be subject to promotion and demotion, so that reward and punishment are clear.
value.literal: The fifth said: officials who govern the people must all be demoted or promoted in order to make rewards and punishments clear.

value.zh: 六曰逃亡代輸，去來年久者，若非伎作，任聽即住。
value.en: Sixth: fugitives whose obligations are being paid by substitutes, and whose absence or return has lasted for years, should be allowed to settle where they are, unless they are registered artisans.
value.literal: The sixth said: for fugitives whose dues are paid by substitutes, and whose coming and going has lasted many years, if they are not artisans, they should be freely allowed to settle where they are.

value.zh: 七曰邊兵逃走，或實陷沒，皆須精檢；
value.en: Seventh: cases of border soldiers who flee, or who have truly been captured or killed, must be carefully investigated;
value.literal: The seventh said: border soldiers who flee, or who in fact have fallen or been lost, must all be carefully examined;

value.zh: 三長及近親，若實隱之，徵其代輸，不隱勿論。
value.en: if the three chiefs or close relatives truly concealed the facts, collect the substitute payments from them; if they did not conceal them, do not prosecute.
value.literal: if the three chiefs and close kin have truly concealed it, collect substitute payments from them; if they did not conceal it, do not prosecute them.

value.zh: 八曰工商世業之戶，復徵租調，無以堪濟，今請免之，使專其業。
value.en: Eighth: hereditary artisan and merchant households are again being charged rents and levies beyond what they can bear. I request that they be exempted so they can concentrate on their work.
value.literal: The eighth said: households whose hereditary occupations are crafts and commerce are again being charged rents and levies and have no means to endure and meet them. I now request that they be exempted, so that they may specialize in their occupations.

value.zh: 九曰三長禁姦，不得隔越相領，戶不滿者，隨近并合。
value.en: Ninth: the three chiefs, in suppressing crime, should not command across boundaries; where there are too few households, they should be merged with nearby units.
value.literal: The ninth said: the three chiefs, in preventing wrongdoing, may not cross boundaries to command one another; where households are insufficient, they should be merged with nearby units.

value.zh: 十曰羽林虎賁，邊方有事，暫可赴戰，常戍宜遣蕃兵代之。
value.en: Tenth: the Yulin and Huben guards may be sent temporarily to fight when there is trouble on the frontier, but regular garrison duty should be assigned to tribal troops in their place.
value.literal: The tenth said: the Yulin and Huben guards may temporarily go to war when there are affairs on the frontier, but for regular garrison duty tribal troops should be sent to replace them.

value.zh: 靈太后下其奏，百僚議之，事有同否。
value.en: Empress Dowager Ling sent his memorial down for discussion by the officials, who agreed on some points and disagreed on others.
value.literal: Empress Dowager Ling sent down his memorial for the hundred officials to discuss, and in the matters there were agreements and disagreements.

value.zh: 時四中郎將兵數寡弱，不足以襟帶京師，澄奏宜以東中帶滎陽郡，南中帶魯陽郡，西中帶恒農郡，北中帶河內郡，選二品、三品親賢兼稱者居之，省非急之作，配以強兵，如此則深根固本、強幹弱枝之義也。
value.en: At the time the four Central Gentleman-General commands had too few weak troops to protect the capital. Cheng proposed that the Eastern Center be linked with Yingyang Commandery, the Southern Center with Luyang, the Western Center with Hengnong, and the Northern Center with Henei; that qualified close and worthy men of the second and third ranks be chosen to hold them; that nonurgent works be reduced; and that strong troops be assigned. This, he said, would deepen the roots, strengthen the base, strengthen the trunk, and weaken the branches.
value.literal: At the time the troops of the four Gentlemen Generals of the Center were few and weak, insufficient to belt and protect the capital. Cheng memorialized that the Eastern Center should take in Yingyang Commandery, the Southern Center Luyang Commandery, the Western Center Hengnong Commandery, and the Northern Center Henei Commandery; that men of the second and third ranks who were close, worthy, and qualified should be selected to occupy them; that nonurgent works should be eliminated; and that strong troops should be assigned. In this way, he said, lay the meaning of deepening the roots and strengthening the foundation, strengthening the trunk and weakening the branches.

value.zh: 靈太后初將從之，後議者不同，乃止。
value.en: Empress Dowager Ling initially intended to follow the proposal, but later the discussants disagreed, so it was dropped.
value.literal: Empress Dowager Ling at first was about to follow this, but later the discussants disagreed, and so it was stopped.

value.zh: 澄又重奏曰：「固本宜強，防微在豫，故雖有文事，不忘武功。
value.en: Cheng memorialized again, "To secure the root, it must be strengthened; to guard against small dangers, one must prepare in advance. Thus even in civil affairs, military power is not forgotten.
value.literal: Cheng again memorialized, "To secure the root it should be strengthened, and prevention of the slight lies in preparation; therefore, even when there are civil affairs, military achievement is not forgotten.

value.zh: 況今南蠻仍獷，北妖頻結，來事難圖，勢同往變。
value.en: How much more now, when the southern Man remain fierce and northern enemies repeatedly combine. Future events are hard to foresee, and the situation resembles past upheavals.
value.literal: How much more now, when the southern Man remain fierce and the northern demons repeatedly form alliances; future events are difficult to plan for, and the situation is the same as past disturbances.

value.zh: 脫暴勃忽起，振動關畿，四府羸卒，何以防擬。
value.en: If a sudden uprising breaks out and shakes the passes and capital region, how can the weak troops of the four offices defend against it?
value.literal: If sudden violence abruptly arises and shakes the passes and capital region, with the weak soldiers of the four offices, how will we defend and prepare?

value.zh: 平康之世，可以寄安，遺之久長，恐非善策。
value.en: In peaceful times one may rely on security, but to leave matters this way for long is not good policy.
value.literal: In an age of peace and health, we may entrust ourselves to security, but to leave it so for a long time, I fear, is not a good plan.

value.zh: 如臣愚見，郎將領兵，兼總民職，省官實祿，於是乎在。
value.en: In my foolish view, the Gentleman Generals should command troops while also overseeing civil duties; this is where offices can be reduced while real salaries are preserved.
value.literal: In my foolish view, that the Gentleman Generals command troops while also overseeing civil duties, and that offices be reduced while real salaries remain, lies precisely here.

value.zh: 求還依前增兵益號，將位既重，則念報亦深，軍郡相依，則表裏俱濟，朝廷無四顧之憂，姦宄絕窺覦之望矣。」
value.en: I ask that we return to the earlier plan of increasing troops and strengthening the titles. If the generals' posts are weighty, their sense of obligation will deepen; if army and commandery depend on one another, inner and outer defenses will both be supplied. The court will have no worries on any side, and criminals will lose hope of taking advantage."
value.literal: I ask that we return to the former system of increasing troops and augmenting titles. Once the generals' positions are weighty, their thought of repaying the state will also be deep; when army and commandery rely on each other, inside and outside will both be aided, the court will have no worries on four sides, and criminals will lose any hope of peering in."

value.zh: 卒不納。
value.en: In the end the proposal was not accepted.
value.literal: In the end it was not accepted.

value.zh: 又以流人初至遠鎮，衣食無資，多有死者，奏并其妻子給糧一歲，從之。
value.en: He also noted that exiles newly sent to distant garrisons lacked clothing and food and often died, so he memorialized that they and their families be given a year's grain. This was approved.
value.literal: He also, because exiles newly arrived at distant garrisons had no resources for clothing and food and many died, memorialized that they, together with their wives and children, be given grain for one year, and this was followed.

value.zh: 尋以疾患，求解任，不許。
value.en: Soon afterward he asked to be relieved because of illness, but this was not allowed.
value.literal: Soon, because of illness, he requested to be relieved of office, but it was not permitted.

value.zh: 蕭衍於浮山斷淮為堰，以灌壽春，乃除使持節、大將軍、大都督、南討諸軍事，勒眾十萬，將出彭宋，尋淮堰自壞，不行。
value.en: When Xiao Yan dammed the Huai at Fushan to flood Shouchun, Cheng was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Grand General, and Grand Commander of the southern campaign armies, with orders to lead one hundred thousand men out through Peng and Song. Soon the Huai dam collapsed on its own, and the campaign did not proceed.
value.literal: When Xiao Yan, at Fushan, cut off the Huai to make a dam in order to flood Shouchun, Cheng was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Grand General, Grand Commander of all armies for the southern campaign, and ordered to command one hundred thousand men and prepare to go out through Peng and Song. Soon the Huai dam broke by itself, and he did not proceed.

value.zh: 澄以北邊鎮將選舉彌輕，恐賊虜闚邊，山陵危迫，奏求重鎮將之選，修警備之嚴，詔不從。
value.en: Cheng believed that commanders for the northern frontier garrisons were being chosen too lightly. Fearing that raiders would threaten the border and endanger the imperial tombs, he memorialized asking that garrison commanders be selected more carefully and defenses tightened, but the edict did not accept this.
value.literal: Because Cheng considered the selection of commanders for the northern frontier garrisons increasingly slight, and feared that rebel captives would peer at the border and the imperial tombs would be endangered, he memorialized requesting that selection of garrison commanders be made weightier and the strictness of warning and defense be repaired, but the edict did not follow it.

value.zh: 賊虜入寇，至於舊都，鎮將多非其人，所在叛亂，犯逼山陵，如澄所慮。
value.en: When the raiders entered and reached the old capital, many garrison commanders proved unfit, rebellions broke out in many places, and the imperial tombs were threatened, exactly as Cheng had feared.
value.literal: When rebel captives entered and raided, reaching the old capital, many garrison commanders were not the right men, rebellions broke out everywhere, and they violated and pressed upon the imperial tombs, just as Cheng had feared.

value.zh: 澄奏都城府寺猶未周悉，今軍旅初寧，無宜發眾，請取諸職人及司州郡縣犯十杖已上百鞭已下收贖之物，絹一匹，輸磚二百，以漸修造。
value.en: Cheng memorialized that the capital's offices and temples were still incomplete, but since the armies had only just settled, the people should not be mobilized. He asked instead to use office laborers and the redemption payments for offenses in Sizhou commanderies and counties punishable by ten strokes to one hundred lashes: each bolt of silk would be commuted to two hundred bricks, so construction could proceed gradually.
value.literal: Cheng memorialized that the offices and temples of the capital city were still not complete; now that military affairs had just become quiet, it was not fitting to mobilize the masses. He requested that they take from various office workers and from the ransom goods paid for offenses in Sizhou commanderies and counties punishable by ten strokes or more and one hundred lashes or less: for one bolt of silk, two hundred bricks should be delivered, gradually to carry out construction.

value.zh: 詔從之。
value.en: The edict approved this.
value.literal: The edict followed this.

value.zh: 太傅、清河王懌表奏其事，遂寢不行。
value.en: The Grand Tutor Yuan Yi, Prince of Qinghe, submitted a memorial about the matter, and it was shelved without being carried out.
value.literal: Grand Tutor Yi, Prince of Qinghe, memorialized on the matter, and it was then set aside and not carried out.

value.zh: 澄又奏曰：「臣聞賞必以道，用防淫人之姦；
value.en: Cheng also memorialized, "I have heard that rewards must follow the Way, to guard against the schemes of corrupt men;
value.literal: Cheng again memorialized, "I have heard that rewards must accord with the Way, to guard against the wickedness of excessive men;

value.zh: 罰不濫及，以戒良士之困。
value.en: punishments must not be indiscriminate, lest good men be driven into distress.
value.literal: punishments must not reach indiscriminately, in order to warn against the distress of good men.

value.zh: 刑者，侀也。
value.en: Punishment is a matter of setting a model.
value.literal: Punishment means modeling.

value.zh: 每垂三宥，秉律執請，不得已而用之。
value.en: One should always extend the three pardons, and only when the law is upheld and the request cannot be granted should punishment be used.
value.literal: One always extends the three pardons, and only when holding the law and presenting the request leaves no alternative is it used.

value.zh: 是故小大之獄，察之以情，一人呼嗟，或虧王道。
value.en: Thus in cases great and small, one examines the circumstances; even one person crying out in grievance can diminish the kingly Way.
value.literal: Therefore, in prisons small and great, cases are examined according to feeling; if one person cries out in sorrow, it may diminish the kingly Way.

value.zh: 刑罰得失，乃興廢之所由也。
value.en: The success or failure of punishments is the source of a state's rise or decline.
value.literal: The success and failure of punishments are the route by which states rise or fall.

value.zh: 竊聞司州牧、高陽王臣雍栲殺奉朝請韓元昭、前門下錄事姚敬賢，雖因公事，理實未盡。
value.en: I have heard privately that Yuan Yong, Minister of Sizhou and Prince of Gaoyang, tortured and killed Han Yuanzhao, Gentleman for Court Audience, and Yao Jingxian, former Recorder of the Chancellery. Although this arose from official business, the facts were not fully investigated.
value.literal: I have privately heard that Yong, Minister of Sizhou and Prince of Gaoyang, tortured and killed Han Yuanzhao, Gentleman for Court Audience, and Yao Jingxian, former Recorder of the Chancellery. Although this arose from official business, in principle the facts were not exhausted.

value.zh: 何者？
value.en: Why do I say this?
value.literal: Why is this?

value.zh: 太平之世，草不橫伐，行葦之感，事驗隆周。
value.en: In an age of great peace, even grasses are not wantonly cut; the compassion shown in "Walking among the Reeds" was proven in the flourishing Zhou.
value.literal: In an age of great peace, even grass is not cut sideways; the feeling of "walking among the reeds" was verified in the flourishing Zhou.

value.zh: 若昭等狀彰，死罪以定，應刑於都市，與眾棄之；
value.en: If the crimes of Yuanzhao and the others were clear and death sentences certain, they should have been executed in the marketplace and cast out before the crowd;
value.literal: If the circumstances of Zhao and the others were manifest and the capital crime fixed, they should have been executed in the marketplace and cast away with the crowd;

value.zh: 如其疑似不分，情理未究，不宜以三清九流之官杖下便死，輕絕民命，傷理敗法。
value.en: if the suspicions had not been distinguished and the facts had not been fully examined, officials of their rank should not have died under the cudgel, their lives lightly cut off in a way that injured principle and ruined law.
value.literal: if suspicion and likeness were not distinguished and the facts and principle not fully examined, it was not fitting for officials of pure rank and regular service to die beneath the staff, lightly cutting off the people's lives and injuring principle and ruining law.

value.zh: 往年州於大市鞭殺五人，及檢贓狀，全無寸尺。
value.en: In a previous year the province flogged five men to death in the great marketplace, and when the alleged stolen goods were investigated there was not the slightest evidence.
value.literal: In a previous year, the province flogged five men to death in the great marketplace, and when the circumstances of stolen goods were inspected, there was not even an inch or foot of evidence.

value.zh: 今復酷害，一至於此。
value.en: Now its cruelty has once again gone this far.
value.literal: Now again cruel harm has once reached this point.

value.zh: 朝野云云，咸懷驚愕。
value.en: Court and countryside are talking, and everyone is shocked.
value.literal: Court and countryside are full of talk, and all harbor shock and alarm.

value.zh: 若殺生在下，虐專於臣，人君之權，安所復用。
value.en: If life and death lie in the hands of subordinates and cruelty is monopolized by ministers, what use remains for the ruler's authority?
value.literal: If killing and giving life are in those below, and cruelty is monopolized by ministers, where can the ruler's authority be used again?

value.zh: 自開古以來，明明之世，未聞斯比也。
value.en: Since antiquity began, in bright and enlightened ages, I have never heard of such a thing.
value.literal: From the opening of antiquity onward, in clear and enlightened ages, I have never heard of anything like this.

value.zh: 武王曰：『吾不以一人之命而易天下。』
value.en: King Wu said, "I would not trade one man's life for all under Heaven."
value.literal: King Wu said, "I would not exchange all under Heaven for the life of one man."

value.zh: 蓋重民命也。
value.en: This was because he valued human life.
value.literal: This was because he valued the people's lives.

value.zh: 請以見事付廷尉推究，驗其為劫之狀，察其栲殺之理，使是非分明，幽魂獲雪。」
value.en: I request that the case be given to the Chamberlain for Law Enforcement to investigate, verify the alleged robbery, and examine the grounds for the torture-killings, so that right and wrong become clear and the dead may be vindicated."
value.literal: I request that the present matter be given to the Chamberlain for Law Enforcement for investigation, to verify the circumstances of their robbery and examine the principle of the torture-killings, so that right and wrong may be made clear and the hidden souls may obtain exoneration."

value.zh: 詔從之。
value.en: The edict approved this.
value.literal: The edict followed this.

value.zh: 澄當官而行，無所回避。
value.en: Cheng acted according to his office and avoided nothing.
value.literal: Cheng acted according to his office and had nothing from which he turned aside or avoided.

value.zh: 又奏墾田授受之制八條，甚有綱貫，大便於時。
value.en: He also memorialized eight provisions on the system for allotting reclaimed fields. They were orderly and coherent, and greatly suited the needs of the time.
value.literal: He also memorialized eight articles on the system for granting and receiving cultivated fields; they had much order and coherence and were greatly convenient at the time.

value.zh: 前來尚書文簿，諸曹須，則出借。
value.en: Previously, when the various bureaus needed documents and registers from the Department of State Affairs, the records were lent out.
value.literal: Previously, when documents and registers of the Department of State Affairs were needed by the various bureaus, they were lent out.

value.zh: 時公車署以理冤事重。
value.en: At the time, the Office of Public Carriages regarded the handling of grievance cases as important.
value.literal: At the time, the Office of Public Carriages considered the handling of grievance cases important.

value.zh: 奏請真案。
value.en: It memorialized requesting the original case files.
value.literal: It memorialized requesting the original case files.

value.zh: 澄執奏以尚書政本，特宜遠慎，故凡所奏事，閣道通之，蓋以祕要之切，防其宣露，寧有古制所重，今反輕之，內猶設禁，外更寬也。
value.en: Cheng insisted in a memorial that the Department of State Affairs was the root of government and had to be handled with special caution. All memorialized matters were transmitted through the palace galleries precisely because secrecy was urgent and disclosure had to be prevented. How could something the ancient system treated as weighty now be treated lightly, keeping restrictions inside while loosening them outside?
value.literal: Cheng firmly memorialized that the Department of State Affairs was the root of government and especially should be treated with far-reaching caution; therefore, all memorialized affairs were transmitted through the gallery passage, precisely because of the urgent importance of secrecy and to guard against their being disclosed. How could something valued by the ancient system now instead be treated lightly, with prohibitions still set inside while outside they were made even looser?

value.zh: 宜繕寫事意，以付公車。
value.en: The substance of the case should be copied out and given to the Office of Public Carriages.
value.literal: The meaning of the matter should be copied out and given to the Office of Public Carriages.

value.zh: 燕鳳 許謙 張袞 崔玄伯 鄧淵
value.en: Biographies of Yan Feng, Xu Qian, Zhang Gun, Cui Xuanbo, and Deng Yuan
value.literal: Yan Feng; Xu Qian; Zhang Gun; Cui Xuanbo; Deng Yuan

value.zh: 張袞，字洪龍，上谷沮陽人也。
value.en: Zhang Gun, styled Honglong, came from Juyang in Shanggu.
value.literal: Zhang Gun, styled Honglong, was a man of Juyang in Shanggu.

value.zh: 祖翼，遼東太守。
value.en: His grandfather Yi had been administrator of Liaodong.
value.literal: His grandfather Yi was Administrator of Liaodong.

value.zh: 父卓，昌黎太守。
value.en: His father Zhuo was administrator of Changli.
value.literal: His father Zhuo was Administrator of Changli.

value.zh: 袞初為郡五官掾，純厚篤實，好學，有文才。
value.en: Gun began as the commandery registrar of five offices — honest, steady, studious, and gifted in letters.
value.literal: Gun at first was the commandery Registrar of Five Offices — pure, thick, and sincere, loving learning, with literary talent.

value.zh: 太祖為代王，選為左長史。
value.en: When Taizu was Prince of Dai, Gun was chosen as left chief of staff.
value.literal: When Taizu was Prince of Dai he was chosen as Left Chief of Staff.

value.zh: 韓麒麟 程駿
value.en: Han Qilin and Cheng Jun
value.literal: Han Qilin, Cheng Jun

value.zh: 二十一年，車駕南伐，顯宗為右軍府長史、征虜將軍、統軍。
value.en: In the twenty-first year, when the emperor marched south on campaign, Xianzong served as chief clerk of the Right Army headquarters, General Who Conquers the Barbarians, and commander of the army.
value.literal: In the twenty-first year, when the imperial carriage marched south on campaign, Xianzong served as chief clerk of the Right Army headquarters, General Who Conquers the Barbarians, and army commander.

value.zh: 軍次赭陽，蕭鸞戍主成公期遣其軍主胡松、高法援等并引蠻賊來擊軍營，顯宗親率拒戰，遂斬法援首。
value.en: When the army halted at Zheyang, Cheng Gongqi, garrison commander under Xiao Luan, sent his commanders Hu Song and Gao Fayuan, among others, together with tribal allies to strike the camp; Xianzong personally led the defense and cut off Fayuan's head.
value.literal: When the army halted at Zheyang, Xiao Luan's garrison commander Cheng Gongqi sent his army commanders Hu Song, Gao Fayuan, and others, together leading tribal raiders to attack the camp; Xianzong personally led the resistance and beheaded Fayuan.

value.zh: 顯宗至新野，高祖詔曰：「卿破賊斬帥，殊益軍勢，朕方攻堅城，何為不作露布也？」
value.en: When Xianzong reached Xinye, Emperor Xiaowen sent an edict: "You broke the enemy and beheaded their commander, greatly strengthening our army's momentum; I am pressing a hard siege — why did you not publish a victory bulletin?"
value.literal: When Xianzong reached Xinye, Emperor Gaozu issued an edict: "You broke the enemy and beheaded their commander, greatly strengthening army morale; I am assaulting a fortified city — why did you not issue a battle report?"

value.zh: 顯宗曰：「臣頃聞鎮南將軍王肅獲賊二三，驢馬數匹，皆為露布，臣在東觀，私每哂之。
value.en: Xianzong said: "I recently heard that General Who Pacifies the South Wang Su captured two or three enemies and a few donkeys and horses, yet still issued victory bulletins; when I served at the Eastern Hall, I privately laughed at that every time.
value.literal: Xianzong said: "Your subject recently heard that General Who Pacifies the South Wang Su captured two or three enemies and several donkeys and horses, yet issued battle reports; when I was at the Eastern Hall for observations, I privately always laughed at this.

value.zh: 近雖仰憑威靈，得摧醜虜，兵寡力弱，擒斬不多。
value.en: Recently, though I leaned on your august power and was able to break the foul enemy, my troops were few and my strength slight; captures and kills were not many.
value.literal: Recently, though relying on your august power I was able to crush the foul enemy, our troops were few and strength weak; captures and kills were not many.

value.zh: 脫復高曳長縑，虛張功捷，尤而效之，其罪彌甚。
value.en: If I now unfurled long silk banners and falsely inflated my achievements, copying that fault and making it my own, my offense would be all the graver.
value.literal: If I again hoisted long silk banners and falsely inflated achievements, committing the same fault and imitating that example, my guilt would be all the greater.

value.zh: 臣所以斂毫卷帛，解上而已。」
value.en: That is why I put away brush and silk and submitted only a plain report."
value.literal: Therefore I folded my brush and rolled up the silk and submitted a simple report, nothing more."

value.zh: 高祖笑曰：「如卿此勳，誠合茅社，須赭陽平定，檢審相酬。」
value.en: Emperor Xiaowen smiled and said: "Merit such as yours truly deserves a fief of earth and altar; once Zheyang is pacified, I shall review the matter and reward you properly."
value.literal: Emperor Gaozu smiled and said: "For merit such as yours, you truly deserve a fief of earth and altar; once Zheyang is pacified, I shall review and reward you accordingly."

value.zh: 新野平，以顯宗為鎮南、廣陽王嘉諮議參軍。
value.en: When Xinye was pacified, Xianzong was appointed consulting adjutant on the staff of Prince Jia of Guangyang under the General Who Pacifies the South.
value.literal: When Xinye was pacified, Xianzong was made consulting adjutant to Prince Jia of Guangyang under the General Who Pacifies the South.

value.zh: 顯宗後上表，頗自矜伐，訴前征勳，詔曰：「顯宗斐然成章，甚可怪責，進退無檢，虧我清風。
value.en: Later Xianzong submitted a memorial, rather full of self-praise, pleading his earlier campaign merit. An edict said: "Xianzong's polished prose is very much to be censured; his conduct lacks restraint in advance and retreat, and it tarnishes our pure ethos.
value.literal: Later Xianzong submitted a memorial, rather self-praising, pleading his prior campaign merit. An edict read: "Xianzong's polished composition is much to be blamed; his advance and retreat lack restraint and damage our pure ethos.

value.zh: 此而不糾，或長弊俗。
value.en: If this is not corrected, corrupt custom may take deeper root.
value.literal: If this is not corrected, corrupt custom may grow.

value.zh: 可付尚書，推列以聞。」
value.en: Let the matter be referred to the Masters of Writing for investigation and report."
value.literal: Let it be referred to the Masters of Writing to investigate and report."

value.zh: 兼尚書張彝奏免顯宗官，詔曰：「顯宗雖浮矯致愆，才猶可用，豈得永棄之也！
value.en: Concurrent Master of Writing Zhang Yi memorialized to dismiss Xianzong from office. An edict said: "Though Xianzong's vanity brought him to fault, his talent is still usable — how can he be cast off forever!
value.literal: Concurrent Master of Writing Zhang Yi memorialized to dismiss Xianzong from office. An edict said: "Though Xianzong's vanity caused fault, his talent is still usable — how can he be abandoned forever!

value.zh: 可以白衣守諮議，展其後效。
value.en: He may continue as adviser in plain clothes and prove his worth hereafter.
value.literal: He may serve as adviser in plain clothes and show his merit hereafter.

value.zh: 但鄙很之性，不足參華，可奪見□，并禁問訊諸王。」
value.en: But his coarse and obstinate nature makes him unfit for elegant company; his privilege of audience may be revoked, and he is forbidden to call upon or inquire after the princes."
value.literal: But his boorish and obstinate nature is unfit for elegant company; his audience privilege may be revoked □, and he is forbidden to call upon or inquire after the princes."

value.zh: 郭祚 張彝
value.en: Guo Zuo; Zhang Yi
value.literal: Guo Zuo; Zhang Yi

value.zh: 彝愛好知己，輕忽下流，非其意者，視之蔑爾。
value.en: Zhang Yi cherished those he knew and looked down on those beneath him; anyone who did not suit him he treated with contempt.
value.literal: Yi loved and favored those he knew well and slighted those of lower rank; those who did not suit his liking he regarded with contempt.

value.zh: 雖疹疾家庭，而志氣彌亮。
value.en: Though illness kept him at home, his resolve burned all the brighter.
value.literal: Though afflicted with illness at home, his spirit was all the brighter.

value.zh: 上表曰：「臣聞元天高朗，尚假列星以助明；
value.en: He memorialized the throne: "I have heard that though primordial Heaven is high and clear, it still borrows the array of stars to help its light;
value.literal: In a memorial he said: "Your servant has heard that though the primordial Heaven is lofty and clear, it still borrows the array of stars to aid its brilliance;

value.zh: 洞庭淵湛，猶藉眾流以增大。
value.en: though Dongting is deep and vast, it still relies on many streams to swell its breadth.
value.literal: though Dongting is deep and vast, it still relies on many streams to enlarge it.

value.zh: 莫不以孤照不詣其幽，獨深未盡其廣。
value.en: Neither solitary light reaches every shadow, nor solitary depth fills every expanse.
value.literal: None can illuminate the hidden with a solitary beam, nor exhaust the breadth with depth alone.

value.zh: 先聖識其若此，必取物以自誡。
value.en: The ancient sages, knowing this, always took things around them as warnings to themselves.
value.literal: The ancient sages, knowing this to be so, invariably took material things as admonitions to themselves.

value.zh: 故堯稱則天，設謗木以曉未明；
value.en: Thus Yao, styled Pattern of Heaven, set up a board for criticism to reveal what was still dark;
value.literal: Thus Yao, styled "the Pattern of Heaven," set up a wooden board for criticism to make known what was unclear;

value.zh: 舜稱盡善，懸諫鼓以規政闕。
value.en: Shun, styled Utmost Goodness, hung a drum for remonstrance to mark what was lacking in government.
value.literal: Shun, styled "Utmost Goodness," hung a remonstrance drum to mark flaws in governance.

value.zh: 虞人獻箴規之旨，盤盂著舉動之銘，庶幾見善而思齊，聞惡以自改。
value.en: Forest keepers offered words of admonition; basins and cups bore inscriptions on conduct—so that seeing good one would strive to match it, and hearing evil one would turn and reform.
value.literal: Forest keepers offered the purpose of admonition and regulation; basins and cups bore inscriptions on conduct—so that upon seeing good one might aspire to emulate it, and upon hearing evil one might reform oneself.

value.zh: 眷眷於悔往之衢，孜孜於不逮之路，用能聲高百王，卓絕中古，經十氏而不渝，歷二千以孤鬱。
value.en: Attentive on the road of repenting the past, tireless on the path of what they had not yet reached—they raised their fame above the hundred kings, stood alone through the middle ages, endured through ten houses without wavering, and shone across two thousand years.
value.literal: Attentive on the path of repenting past errors, diligent on the road of what one has not yet attained—thus their fame towered above the hundred kings, transcendent through the middle antiquity, enduring through ten dynasties without change, spanning two thousand years in solitary eminence.

value.zh: 伏惟太祖撥亂，弈代重光。
value.en: I humbly consider that Grand Ancestor quelled the chaos, and dynasty after dynasty renewed the imperial light.
value.literal: I humbly consider that Grand Ancestor [Emperor Taiwu] quelled the chaos, and generation after generation renewed the imperial splendor.

value.zh: 世祖以不世之才，開盪函夏；
value.en: Emperor Shizu, possessing extraordinary talent, expanded rule over the Central Plains.
value.literal: Emperor Shizu, with matchless talent, opened and swept across the Central Plains.

value.zh: 顯祖以溫明之德，潤沃九區。
value.en: Emperor Xianzu, with his gentle and luminous virtue, nourished all the realm.
value.literal: Emperor Xianzu, with warm and bright virtue, moistened and enriched the nine regions.

value.zh: [2]高祖大聖臨朝，經營云始，未明求衣，日昃忘食，開翦荊棘，徙御神縣，更新風軌，冠帶朝流。
value.en: Emperor Gaozu the great sage came to the throne and began his labors from the very start—rising before dawn and forgetting meals at dusk—cutting away brambles, moving the capital to the sacred heartland, renewing laws and customs, and drawing the civilized world to court.
value.literal: Emperor Gaozu the great sage attended court, beginning his efforts at the start; rising before daylight and forgetting to eat at sunset, he cleared thorns and brambles, moved the capital to the sacred heartland, renewed customs and institutions, and drew the girdled and capped to court.

value.zh: 海東雜種之渠，衡南異服之帥，沙西氊頭之戎，漠北辮髮之虜，重譯納貢，請吏稱藩。
value.en: Tribal leaders from the eastern seas, southern chiefs in exotic dress, felt-hatted barbarians west of the sands, and braided-haired peoples north of the desert—all sent tribute through successive interpreters and requested imperial administrators, styling themselves as vassals.
value.literal: Chiefs of mixed tribes east of the sea, chieftains in strange dress south of Heng, felt-hatted barbarians west of the sands, and braided-haired enemies north of the desert—all came through multiple translations to offer tribute and requested officials, styling themselves as vassals.

value.zh: 積德懋於夏殷，富仁盛於周漢，澤教既周，武功亦匝。
value.en: Their accumulated virtue surpassed that of the Xia and Shang, their benevolence exceeded that of the Zhou and Han; civilizing influence was complete, and military achievements likewise comprehensive.
value.literal: Accumulated virtue surpassing Xia and Yin, abundant benevolence exceeding Zhou and Han—benevolent instruction was complete, and martial achievements likewise comprehensive.

value.zh: 猶且發明詔，思求直士，信是蒼生薦言之秋，祝史陳辭之日。
value.en: They even issued enlightened decrees seeking upright officials—it was truly the season when the people might offer counsel and when the ritual officials might speak their minds.
value.literal: Moreover they issued bright edicts seeking upright men—it was truly the season for the common people to offer advice and for the prayer-officers to present their words.

value.zh: 況臣家自奉國八十餘年，紆金鏘玉，及臣四世。
value.en: Moreover, my family has served the state for over eighty years, honored with gold seals and jade insignia, spanning four generations down to me.
value.literal: Moreover, my family has served the state for over eighty years, adorned with gold seals and jade insignia, extending to four generations including myself.

value.zh: 過以小才，藉蔭出仕，學慚專門，武闕方略，早荷先帝眷仗之恩，末蒙陛下不遺之施。
value.en: I came to office beyond my modest abilities through inherited privilege; I lacked specialized learning and military strategy. I was early favored by the late emperor and later found favor with Your Majesty despite my unworthiness.
value.literal: I overstepped with my small talent, entered office through inherited favor; ashamed in learning for lacking specialization and in warfare for lacking strategy—I early received the previous emperor's trusting favor and finally Your Majesty's gracious consideration without abandonment.

value.zh: [3]侍則出入兩都，[4]官歷納言常伯，忝牧秦藩，號兼安撫。
value.en: I attended at court, moving between the two capitals; I served as Chief Counselor and Regular Grandee, and shamefully governed the Qin domain with the concurrent title of Pacification Commissioner.
value.literal: Attending at court I moved between the two capitals; my offices included Chief Counselor and Regular Grandee, and I shamefully governed the Qin domain with the concurrent title of Pacification Commissioner.

value.zh: 實思碎首膏原，仰酬二朝之惠；
value.en: I truly wished to give my life to repay the kindness of two emperors.
value.literal: Truly I wished to smash my head and smear my blood on the plain, looking up to repay the grace of two reigns.

value.zh: 輕塵碎石，遠增嵩岱之高。
value.en: Though insignificant as dust or pebbles, I hoped from afar to add to the stature of Mount Song and Mount Tai.
value.literal: Light as dust and broken stone, I hoped from afar to increase the height of Mount Song and Mount Tai.

value.zh: 輒私訪舊書，竊觀圖史，其帝皇興起之元，配天隆家之業，修造益民之奇，龍麟雲鳳之瑞，卑宮愛物之仁，釋網改祝之澤，前歌後舞之應，囹圄寂寥之美，可為輝風景行者，輒謹編丹青，以標睿範。
value.en: I privately consulted ancient texts and historical records, and for accounts of emperors' founding achievements, dynastic glory endorsed by Heaven, marvelous works benefiting the people, auspicious omens of dragons, qilin, clouds, and phoenixes, humane governance through frugal palaces and care for creatures, merciful policies of sparing the net and reforming sacrifices, popular rejoicing, and the virtue of empty prisons—all that could inspire and instruct—I carefully compiled them in illustrated form to mark the wise standard.
value.literal: I then privately consulted old books and secretly viewed illustrated histories; of emperors' rise to power, enterprises matching Heaven and elevating families, marvelous works benefiting the people, auspicious signs of dragons, qilin, clouds, and phoenixes, the benevolence of humble palaces and love of creatures, the grace of releasing nets and changing prayers, the response of singing before and dancing behind, and the beauty of empty prisons—all that could illuminate and inspire—I carefully compiled in paintings to mark the wise standard.

value.zh: 至如太康好田，遇窮后迫禍；
value.en: Taikang loved hunting and met disaster when the end came and his empress brought ruin.
value.literal: King Taikang loved hunting and met disaster when the end came and his empress brought ruin.

value.zh: 武乙逸禽，罹震雷暴酷；
value.en: King Wuyi amused himself with flying birds and was struck down by thunder in violent punishment.
value.literal: King Wuyi amused himself with flying birds and suffered violent thunder in punishment.

value.zh: 夏桀淫亂，南巢有非命之誅；
value.en: Xia Jie was debauched and tyrannical; at Nanqiao he met an untimely death.
value.literal: Xia Jie was licentious and disorderly; at Nanqiao there was execution not by fate.

value.zh: 殷紂昏酣，牧野有倒戈之陳；
value.en: King Zhou of Yin was dissolute and drunk; at Muye his troops turned their weapons against him.
value.literal: King Zhou of Yin was muddled and drunken; at Muye there was the array of turned spears.

value.zh: 周厲逐獸，滅不旋踵；
value.en: King Li of Zhou obsessed over hunting; his ruin followed almost immediately.
value.literal: King Li of Zhou chased beasts; destruction came without turning the heel.

value.zh: 幽王遇惑，死亦相尋；
value.en: King You was beguiled into error; death soon followed in turn.
value.literal: King You met deception; death followed in succession.

value.zh: 暨於漢成失御，亡新篡奪；
value.en: Later came Han Chengdi's loss of control and Wang Mang's usurpation.
value.literal: Later came Han Chengdi's loss of control and Wang Mang's usurpation.

value.zh: 桓靈不綱，魏武遷鼎；
value.en: Emperors Huan and Ling neglected governance; Cao Cao moved the imperial seat.
value.literal: Emperors Huan and Ling lacked discipline; Cao Cao moved the imperial seat.

value.zh: 晉惠闇弱，骨肉相屠，終使聰曜鴞視并州，勒虎狼據燕趙：如此之輩，罔不畢載。
value.en: Emperor Hui of Jin was weak and muddled; his kin slaughtered one another, ultimately allowing Liu Cong and Liu Yao to covet Bingzhou like owls and Shi Le to wolf-like occupy Yan and Zhao—all such cases are fully recorded.
value.literal: Emperor Hui of Jin was dim and weak; kin slaughtered one another, ultimately allowing Liu Cong and Liu Yao to owl-watch Bingzhou and Shi Le to wolf-like occupy Yan and Zhao—all such types are without exception fully recorded.

value.zh: 起元庖犧，終於晉末，凡十六代，百二十八帝，歷三千二百七年，雜事五百八十九，合成五卷，名曰歷帝圖，亦謗木、諫鼓、虞人、盤盂之類。
value.en: From Fuxi at the beginning to the end of Jin—sixteen dynasties, 128 emperors, 3,207 years, and 589 miscellaneous records—compiled into five volumes titled Chronicle of Emperors, akin to the remonstrance boards, advice drums, forest keepers, and inscribed basins of old.
value.literal: Beginning from Fuxi at the origin and ending at the end of Jin—in all sixteen dynasties, 128 emperors, spanning 3,207 years, with 589 miscellaneous matters—compiled into five volumes titled Chronicle of Emperors, akin to remonstrance boards, advice drums, forest keepers, and inscribed basins of old.

value.zh: 脫蒙置御坐之側，時復披覽，冀或起予左右，上補未萌。
value.en: If it might be placed beside Your Majesty's seat for occasional reading, I hope it may occasionally awaken me at your side and help remedy troubles before they arise.
value.literal: If I am fortunate enough to have it placed beside the imperial seat for occasional reading, I hope it may occasionally awaken me at your side and help remedy troubles before they arise.

value.zh: 伏願陛下遠惟宗廟之憂，近存黎民之念，取其賢君，棄其惡主，則微臣雖沉淪地下，無異乘雲登天矣。」
value.en: I humbly pray Your Majesty will heed distant concerns for the ancestral temple and keep near in mind the welfare of the people, taking the worthy rulers as models and rejecting the wicked—then though I lie buried underground, it would be as if I ascended to heaven on clouds."
value.literal: I humbly wish Your Majesty would far consider the ancestors' concerns and near preserve thoughts of the people, taking the worthy rulers and discarding the evil ones—then though I sink underground, it would be no different from riding clouds to ascend heaven."

value.zh: 世宗善之。
value.en: Emperor Xuanwu approved it.
value.literal: Emperor Shizong approved it.

value.zh: 史臣曰：郭祚才幹敏實，有世務之長，高祖經綸之始，獨在勤勞之地，居官任事，動靜稱述。
value.en: The historian writes: Guo Zuo was talented, practical, and quick, skilled in affairs of state; at the outset of Emperor Wen's great enterprise he alone bore the heaviest burdens, and in every office his conduct won praise.
value.literal: The historiographer says: Guo Zuo was talented, capable, and diligent in substance, with strengths in worldly affairs; at the beginning of Emperor Gaozu's grand planning he alone stood in the realm of strenuous labor—in office and charged with duties, his conduct in motion and rest was praised.

value.zh: 張彝風力謇謇，有王臣之氣，銜命擁旄，風聲猶在。
value.en: Zhang Yi was forceful and upright, with the air of a true minister of the throne; entrusted with command and banner, his reputation endures still.
value.literal: Zhang Yi was forceful and upright, with the bearing of a king's minister; bearing credentials and waving banners, his renown still stands.

value.zh: 並魏氏器能之臣乎？
value.en: Were they not both able servants of Wei?
value.literal: Were they not both capable ministers of Wei?

value.zh: 遭隨有命，俱嬰世禍，悲哉！
value.en: Subject to the turns of fate, both were struck down by the calamities of their age—how tragic!
value.literal: Meeting fate as it followed, both suffered calamities of the age—how tragic!

value.zh: 始均才志未申，惜也。
value.en: Shijun's talent and ambition were never fully realized—a pity.
value.literal: Shijun's talents and aspirations were unfulfilled—a pity.

value.zh: 蕭瑀瑀從子:鈞 鈞兄子:嗣業 瓘子:嵩 嵩子:華 嵩孫:復 華孫:俛 華孫:倣 倣子:廩 復曾孫:遘 瑀曾孫:定
value.en: Xiao Yu; his nephew's son Jun; Jun's elder brother's son Siye; Guan's son Song; Song's son Hua; Song's grandson Fu; Hua's grandsons Mian and Fang; Fang's son Lin; Fu's great-grandson Gou; and Yu's great-grandson Ding.
value.literal: Xiao Yu; Yu's nephew's son: Jun; Jun's elder brother's son: Siye; Guan's son: Song; Song's son: Hua; Song's grandson: Fu; Hua's grandson: Mian; Hua's grandson: Fang; Fang's son: Lin; Fu's great-grandson: Gou; Yu's great-grandson: Ding.

value.zh: 普王為襄漢元帥，進復戶部尚書、統軍長史。
value.en: When the Prince of Pu was made grand marshal of Xiang-Han, Fu was promoted to Minister of Revenue and chief of staff for the unified command.
value.literal: When the Prince of Pu was grand marshal of Xiang and Han, Fu was advanced to Minister of Revenue and Chief of Staff for the unified army.

value.zh: 舊制謂「行軍長史」，德宗以復父諱更之。
value.en: The old title had been "campaign chief of staff"; Dezong changed it to avoid Fu's father's name (Heng).
value.literal: The old regulation called the post "campaign chief of staff"; Emperor Dezong, because of Fu's father's taboo name, changed the title.

value.zh: 未行，扈狩奉天。
value.en: Before he could depart, the court fled to Fengtian.
value.literal: Before he set out, he accompanied the hunt at Fengtian.

value.zh: 帝惡庳隘，欲西如鳳翔依張鎰。
value.en: The emperor found Fengtian cramped and wished to move west to Fengxiang and Zhang Yi.
value.literal: The emperor disliked the low and narrow place and wished to go west to Fengxiang to rely on Zhang Yi.

value.zh: 復曰：「鳳翔乃泚舊兵，今泚悖亂，當有同惡者。
value.en: Fu said, "Fengxiang was Zhu Ci's old command. Now that Zhu Ci has rebelled, there will be men who share his cause.
value.literal: Fu said: "Fengxiang was Zhu Ci's old troops; now Zhu Ci rebels against order—there should be those of like wicked intent.

value.zh: 雖鎰，臣畏不免。」
value.en: Even with Zhang Yi, I fear we would not be safe."
value.literal: Even Zhang Yi—your servant fears we would not escape harm."

value.zh: 帝曰：「朕業行，留一日以驗爾言！」
value.en: The emperor said, "We are already on the march—stay one day and we shall see if you are right."
value.literal: The emperor said: "We are already on the road—stay one day to verify your words!"

value.zh: 俄而鎰為李楚琳所害，於是拜吏部尚書、同中書門下平章事。
value.en: Within a day Zhang Yi was murdered by Li Chulin, and Fu was made Minister of Personnel and participant in policy deliberation.
value.literal: Soon Zhang Yi was killed by Li Chulin; thereupon Fu was appointed Minister of Personnel with concurrent participation in Council deliberation.

value.zh: 興元初，進門下侍郎。
value.en: In early Xingyuan (784) he was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery.
value.literal: At the beginning of Xingyuan he advanced to Vice Director of the Chancellery.

value.zh: 初，淮南陳少游左附李希烈，而張鎰判官韋皋殺邠、隴叛卒，不應楚琳。
value.en: Chen Shaoyou of Huainan had sided with Li Xilie, while Wei Gao, aide to Zhang Yi, executed the Bin-Long mutineers and refused to follow Li Chulin.
value.literal: At first Chen Shaoyou of Huainan leaned in support of Li Xilie, while Zhang Yi's aide Wei Gao killed the mutinous troops of Bin and Long and did not respond to Chu Lin.

value.zh: 復還執政，建言：「陛下反正，功臣已貴矣，唯甄善汰惡為未明。
value.en: Back in power, Fu said, "Your Majesty has restored order and rewarded the loyal, but you have not yet distinguished the worthy from the wicked.
value.literal: When Fu returned to hold power, he offered counsel: "Your Majesty has returned to the right path; meritorious servants are already honored—only sorting the good and culling the wicked is not yet clear.

value.zh: 少遊位將相，首臣賊，皋名淺官下，獨挺挺抗忠。
value.en: Shaoyou holds high rank yet led the way in serving the rebel; Gao is obscure in rank yet stood alone in loyalty.
value.literal: Shaoyou holds the rank of general and chief minister, yet was foremost in serving the rebel; Gao's name is shallow and his office low, yet alone he stands tall in loyal resistance.

value.zh: 如以皋代少遊，則天下嘹然知逆順之理。」
value.en: If Gao replaced Shaoyou, all the realm would clearly see the difference between loyal and traitor."
value.literal: If Gao were used to replace Shaoyou, then the empire would ringingly know the principle of rebellion and submission."

value.zh: 帝許之。
value.en: The emperor agreed.
value.literal: The emperor approved.

value.zh: 復出，中官馬欽緒揖宰相劉從一，附耳語，既而從一密諗復曰：「有詔與公議向所奏，不欲李勉、盧翰聞知。」
value.en: As Fu left, the eunuch Ma Qinxu bowed to Chief Minister Liu Congyi and whispered. Congyi then told Fu privately, "The emperor wishes to discuss your proposal with you alone; Li Mian and Lu Han are not to know."
value.literal: When Fu went out, the eunuch Ma Qinxu bowed to the chief minister Liu Congyi and spoke in his ear; presently Congyi secretly informed Fu: "There is an edict to discuss with you what was just memorialized; we do not wish Li Mian and Lu Han to hear of it."

value.zh: 復曰：「堯、舜有'僉曰'之言，朝廷大事尚當謀及公卿。
value.en: Fu replied, "Even Yao and Shun said 'the multitude proposes.' Great matters of state should be discussed with the chief ministers.
value.literal: Fu said: "Yao and Shun had the saying 'the multitude said'; great affairs of court ought still to be deliberated with the chief ministers and grandees.

value.zh: 如勉等非其人，當罷去。
value.en: If Li Mian and the others are unfit, dismiss them.
value.literal: If Mian and the rest are not the right men, they ought to be dismissed and removed.

value.zh: 既曰宰相，而謀議可獨避之乎？
value.en: But if they are chief ministers, how can state business be kept from them?
value.literal: Since they are called chief ministers, how can counsel and deliberation be deliberately kept from them alone?

value.zh: 今與公行此或可，第恐浸以生常，政由是敝。」
value.en: I might yield to you this once, but I fear it will become habit—and government will suffer for it."
value.literal: I might yield to you this once, but I fear it will become habit—and government will suffer for it."

value.zh: 從一以聞，帝不悅。
value.en: Congyi reported Fu's words; the emperor was displeased.
value.literal: Congyi reported this; the emperor was displeased.

value.zh: 復辭疾上政事，許之。
value.en: Fu pleaded illness and resigned from office; the request was granted.
value.literal: Fu pleaded illness and submitted his governmental affairs; it was granted.

value.zh: 定，字梅臣，瑀曾孫。
value.en: Ding, styled Meichen, was Yu's great-grandson.
value.literal: Ding, style name Meichen, was Yu's great-grandson.

value.zh: 以廕起家陝州參軍事、金城丞。
value.en: He entered service through hereditary privilege as adjutant at Shanzhou and magistrate of Jincheng.
value.literal: By yin privilege he began his career as military adjutant of Shan Prefecture and magistrate of Jincheng.

value.zh: 蒞事清挺。
value.en: In office he was incorruptible and stern.
value.literal: In conducting affairs he was pure and upright.

value.zh: 選補黜陟使裴遵慶表為判官，還調萬年主簿。
value.en: Pei Zunqing, commissioner for personnel review, recommended him as aide; he was later posted as chief clerk of Wannian County.
value.literal: Personnel selection and promotion-and-demotion commissioner Pei Zunqing recommended him as case officer; on return he was transferred to chief clerk of Wannian.

value.zh: 歷左右司郎中。
value.en: He rose to director in the Left and Right Secretariats.
value.literal: He successively served as director in the Left and Right Departments of the Secretariat.

value.zh: 為元載所惡，外遷袁、潤等六州刺史。
value.en: Yuan Zai disliked him and had him sent out to serve as prefect of six prefectures, including Yuan and Run.
value.literal: Hated by Yuan Zai, he was transferred outward as prefect of six prefectures including Yuan and Run.

value.zh: 大曆中，有司差天下刺史治最，定與常州蕭復、豪州張鎰為第一，而劭桑稼，均賦稅，業徠遊口，在鎰、復右。
value.en: In the Dali era, when the ministry ranked governors for outstanding administration, Ding stood first alongside Xiao Fu of Changzhou and Zhang Yi of Haozhou. Yet in promoting agriculture, equalizing taxes, and settling displaced people, he outranked both.
value.literal: In the Dali era, the relevant office ranked governors nationwide for best administration; Ding together with Xiao Fu of Chang Prefecture and Zhang Yi of Hao Prefecture were first—but in encouraging mulberry and grain, equalizing taxes and levies, and building up the wandering population, he stood above Yi and Fu.

value.zh: 遷戶部侍郎、太常卿。
value.en: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue and Minister of Ceremonies.
value.literal: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue and Minister of Ceremonial.

value.zh: 硃泚泚反，詭姓名為張誕，匿裏中，與蔣沇不浼於賊。
value.en: When Zhu Ci rebelled, Ding assumed the false name Zhang Yan, hid among the people, and—along with Jiang Yan—kept himself unstained by the rebels.
value.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled, [Ding] disguised his name as Zhang Yan, hid in the countryside, and together with Jiang Yan did not defile themselves before the rebels.

value.zh: 事平，擢太子少師。
value.en: After order was restored, he was made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
value.literal: When the affair was settled, he was promoted to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

value.zh: 卒，年七十七，贈太子太師。
value.en: He died at seventy-seven and was posthumously honored as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
value.literal: He died at age seventy-seven; posthumously enfeoffed Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

value.zh: ◎蘇尹畢李鄭王許潘倪席齊蘇向，雍州藍田人。
value.en: In the biographies of Su, Yin, Bi, Li, Zheng, Wang, Xu, Pan, Ni, Xi, and Qi, Su Xiang came from Lantian in Yong Prefecture.
value.literal: Su, Yin, Bi, Li, Zheng, Wang, Xu, Pan, Ni, Xi, and Qi: Su Xiang was a native of Lantian in Yong Prefecture.

value.zh: 中明經第，調鄠尉。
value.en: He passed the Mingjing examination and was posted as aide at Hu County.
value.literal: He placed in the Mingjing examination and was appointed aide at Hu.

value.zh: 時李義琰為雍州長史，鄠多訟，日至長史府，恦裁決明辦，自是無訴者。
value.en: Li Yiyan was then chief secretary of Yong Prefecture. Hu County was rife with lawsuits, and people came every day to the chief secretary's office. Xiang's rulings were lucid and decisive, and after that there were no more complainants.
value.literal: At that time Li Yiyan was chief secretary of Yong Prefecture; Hu had many lawsuits, and people came daily to the chief secretary's office — Xiang's judgments were clear and decisive, and from then on there were no litigants.

value.zh: 義琰異之，顧聽事曰：「此公坐也，恨吾齒晚，不及見。」
value.en: Yiyan was struck by his ability. Glancing toward the reception hall, he said, "That is this gentleman's seat — I only wish I had not grown old so soon and could have known him earlier."
value.literal: Yiyan marveled at him, glanced toward the hall and said, "This is the gentleman's seat; I regret my years came late and I could not meet him sooner."

value.zh: 澣孫抗。
value.en: Huan's grandson Kang.
value.literal: Huan's grandson Kang.

value.zh: 抗字遐舉，少值天寶亂，奉母夫人隱會稽。
value.en: Kang, courtesy name Xiaju, in youth encountered the Tianbao turmoil and supported his mother in seclusion in Kuaiji.
value.literal: Kang, courtesy name Xiaju, in youth encountered the Tianbao turmoil and supported his mother in seclusion in Kuaiji.

value.zh: 壽州刺史張鎰辟署幕府。
value.en: Shou Prefecture prefect Zhang Yi recruited him to his staff.
value.literal: Shou Prefecture prefect Zhang Yi recruited him to his staff.

value.zh: 抗吏事閑敏，有文雅，從鎰鎮江西。
value.en: Kang was quick and adept in office affairs and had literary refinement. He followed Yi to garrison Jiangxi.
value.literal: Kang was quick and adept in office affairs and had literary refinement; he followed Yi to garrison Jiangxi.

value.zh: 及以宰相領鳳翔，奏署監察御史。
value.en: When Yi as chief minister also held Fengxiang he memorialized to appoint Kang investigating censor.
value.literal: When Yi as chief minister also held Fengxiang he memorialized to appoint Kang investigating censor.

value.zh: 李楚琳亂，奔奉天，授侍御史，遷戶部員外郎。
value.en: When Li Chulin rebelled he fled to Fengtian, was appointed attending censor, and was transferred to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.
value.literal: When Li Chulin rebelled he fled to Fengtian, was appointed attending censor, and was transferred to vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.

value.zh: 蕭復引為江淮宣慰判官。
value.en: Xiao Fu brought him in as judge on the Jiang-Huai pacification commission.
value.literal: Xiao Fu brought him in as judge on the Jiang-Huai pacification commission.

value.zh: 德宗自梁、洋還，財用大屈，鹽鐵使元琇薦抗材，改倉部郎中，斡鹽利。
value.en: When Emperor Dezong returned from Liang and Yang finances were greatly strained, Salt and Iron Commissioner Yuan Xiu recommended Kang's talent. He was made director in the Granary Section and managed salt profits.
value.literal: When Dezong returned from Liang and Yang finances were greatly strained, Salt and Iron Commissioner Yuan Xiu recommended Kang's talent; he was changed to director in the Granary Section and managed salt profits.

value.zh: 俄為水陸運副使，護漕江淮，給京師。
value.en: Soon he became deputy commissioner for water and land transport, supervised grain transport on the Jiang and Huai, and supplied the capital.
value.literal: Soon he became deputy commissioner for water and land transport, supervised grain transport on the Jiang and Huai, and supplied the capital.

value.zh: 歷諫議大夫，坐小累，為處州刺史。
value.en: He served as grand remonstrator. For a minor offense he became prefect of Chu Prefecture.
value.literal: He served as grand remonstrator; for a minor offense he became prefect of Chu.

value.zh: 歷蘇州，徙潭州觀察使，召為給事中，遷河南尹，進太常卿，以中書侍郎同中書門下平章事。
value.en: He served in Su Prefecture, was moved to investigating commissioner of Tan Prefecture, was summoned as palace attendant, transferred to intendant of Henan, advanced to chief of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and as vice minister of the Secretariat became co-equal with the chief ministers of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
value.literal: He served in Su Prefecture, was moved to investigating commissioner of Tan Prefecture, was summoned as attendant within the palace gates, transferred to intendant of Henan, advanced to chief of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and as vice minister of the Secretariat became co-equal with the chief ministers of the Secretariat and Chancellery.

value.zh: 裴崔盧李王嚴
value.en: Pei, Cui, Lu, Li, Wang, and Yan
value.literal: Pei, Cui, Lu, Li, Wang, Yan

value.zh: 武在蜀頗放肆，用度無藝，或一言之悅，賞至百萬。
value.en: In Shu, Wu was quite unrestrained. His spending knew no bounds, and sometimes a single pleasing remark would earn a reward of as much as a million cash.
value.literal: Wu in Shu was quite unrestrained; his expenditures knew no limit, and sometimes for a single pleasing remark he would reward as much as a million.

value.zh: 蜀雖號富饒，而峻掊亟斂，閭裏為空，然虜亦不敢近境。
value.en: Although Shu was known as rich and fertile, he taxed it harshly and relentlessly until whole neighborhoods were drained empty. Even so, the enemy did not dare approach the border.
value.literal: Although Shu was called rich and fertile, he harshly scraped and urgently levied taxes until neighborhoods were emptied; yet the barbarians also did not dare approach the border.

value.zh: 梓州刺史章彜始為武判官，因小忿殺之。
value.en: Zhang Yi, prefect of Zizhou, had once served as Wu's aide. Over a minor quarrel Wu had him killed.
value.literal: Zhang Yi, Prefect of Zizhou, had first served as Wu's judge; over a small grievance Wu killed him.

value.zh: 琯以故宰相為巡內刺史，武慢倨不為禮。
value.en: Fang Guan, a former chancellor, came as an itinerant inspector within the circuit, but Wu treated him with arrogant disrespect.
value.literal: Fang Guan, as a former chancellor, served as an itinerant inspector within the circuit; Wu was arrogant and did not show him courtesy.

value.zh: 最厚杜甫，然欲殺甫數矣。
value.en: He was closest to Du Fu, yet more than once he wanted to kill him.
value.literal: He was closest to Du Fu, yet several times he wanted to kill Fu.

value.zh: 李白為《蜀道難》者，乃為房與杜危之也。
value.en: Li Bai wrote "Hard Road to Shu" to warn Fang Guan and Du Fu of the danger they faced.
value.literal: That Li Bai wrote "Hard Road to Shu" was to warn Fang and Du of danger.

value.zh: 永泰初卒，母哭，且曰：「而今而後，吾知免為官婢矣。」
value.en: He died at the beginning of the Yongtai era. His mother wept and said, "From now on I know I am spared becoming a government maidservant."
value.literal: At the beginning of Yongtai he died. His mother wept and said: "From now on, I know I am spared becoming a government maidservant."

value.zh: 年四十，贈尚書左僕射。
value.en: He was forty years old. He was posthumously appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
value.literal: He was forty years old; posthumously appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

value.zh: 梁曾，字貢父，燕人。
value.en: Liang Ceng, whose courtesy name was Gongfu, came from the Yan region.
value.literal: Liang Ceng, styled Gongfu, was a man of Yan.

value.zh: 祖守正，父德，皆以曾貴，贈安定郡公。
value.en: Because of Ceng's prominence, both his grandfather Shouzheng and his father De were posthumously ennobled as Dukes of Anding.
value.literal: His grandfather Shouzheng and his father De, both because of Ceng's eminence, were posthumously enfeoffed as Dukes of Anding.

value.zh: 曾少好學，日記書數千言。
value.en: From childhood Ceng loved study and could commit several thousand characters to memory each day.
value.literal: Ceng from youth loved learning; each day he could memorize several thousand characters in writing.

value.zh: 中統四年，以翰林學士承旨王鶚薦，辟中書左三部令史，三轉為中書省掾。
value.en: In Zhongtong 4 (1263), on the recommendation of Wang E, Grand Preceptor of the Hanlin Academy, he was appointed clerk of the Secretariat's left three departments and, after three promotions, rose to secretary in the Central Secretariat.
value.literal: In the fourth year of Zhongtong, on the recommendation of Hanlin Academician Grand Preceptor Wang E, he was summoned as a clerk of the Left Three Departments of the Central Secretariat, and after three promotions became a secretary of the Central Secretariat.

value.zh: 至元十年，用累考及格，授雲南諸路行省都事，佩銀符。
value.en: In Zhiyuan 10 (1273), having passed the cumulative examinations, he was made chief administrator of the Yunnan regional secretariat and granted a silver tally.
value.literal: In the tenth year of Zhiyuan, through accumulated examinations passing the standard, he was appointed Chief Administrator of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat for All Circuits, wearing a silver tally.

value.zh: 久之，升員外郎。
value.en: After a time he was promoted to vice director.
value.literal: After some time he was promoted to Vice Director.

value.zh: 十五年，轉同知廣南西道左右兩江宣撫司事。
value.en: In year 15 he was transferred to associate commissioner of the pacification commission for the left and right two rivers of western Guangnan.
value.literal: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to serve as Associate Commissioner of the Pacification Commission for the Left and Right Two Rivers of Western Guangnan Circuit.

value.zh: 明年，除知南陽府。
value.en: The next year he was appointed prefect of Nanyang.
value.literal: The following year he was appointed Prefect of Nanyang.

value.zh: 唐、鄧二屬州為襄陽府所奪，曾按圖經、稽國製以聞，事得復舊。
value.en: The subordinate prefectures of Tang and Deng had been absorbed by Xiangyang; Ceng checked the gazetteers and national regulations, reported the case, and jurisdiction was restored as before.
value.literal: The two subordinate prefectures Tang and Deng had been seized by Xiangyang Prefecture; Ceng consulted the gazetteers and examined the national regulations, reported the matter, and the former arrangement was restored.

value.zh: 南陽在宋末為邊鄙，桑柘未成，而歲賦絲，民甚苦之，曾請折輸布，民便之。
value.en: At the end of the Song Nanyang had been a border district where mulberry groves were not yet established, yet the annual tax was levied in silk, which greatly burdened the people; Ceng petitioned to substitute cloth, to their relief.
value.literal: Nanyang at the end of the Song had been a frontier region; mulberry and catalpa were not yet established, yet the annual levy was in silk, and the people suffered greatly; Ceng requested conversion of the tribute to cloth, to the people's convenience.

value.zh: 至治元年，英宗即位，帖木迭兒復相，約辭職不出。
value.en: In Zhizhi 1 (1321), when Emperor Yingzong acceded, Temür returned as chancellor; Yue resigned and stayed home.
value.literal: In the first year of Zhizhi, Emperor Yingzong took the throne; Temür again became chancellor; Yue resigned and did not come forth.

value.zh: 二年，以年七十致仕。
value.en: In year 2, at seventy, he retired.
value.literal: In the second year, at age seventy he retired from office.

value.zh: 三年，丞相拜住一新政務，尊禮老臣，傳詔起約，復拜集賢大學士，商議中書省事，以其祿居家，每日一至中書省議事，至治之政，多所參酌。
value.en: In year 3 Chancellor Bayiju reformed the government, honored veteran ministers, and recalled Yue as Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies to advise on Secretariat affairs; living at home on his salary, he came daily to deliberate, and Zhizhi policy owed much to him.
value.literal: In the third year Chancellor Bayiju undertook a new administration, honored old ministers, and by transmitted edict raised Yue; he was again appointed Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies to deliberate on Central Secretariat affairs, living at home on his salary, coming once each day to the Central Secretariat to deliberate on affairs; Zhizhi policies were largely shaped by his counsel.

value.zh: 又嘗奉詔與中書省官及他舊臣，條定國初以來律令，名曰《大元通制》，頒行天下。
value.en: He also helped codify laws since the founding of the dynasty into the Comprehensive Regulations of the Great Yuan, promulgated empire-wide.
value.literal: He also once received an edict, together with Central Secretariat officials and other old ministers, to itemize and fix laws and ordinances from the founding of the state onward, entitled Comprehensive Regulations of the Great Yuan, and promulgate them throughout the empire.

value.zh: 朝廷議罷征東省，立三韓省，制式如他省，詔下中書雜議，約對曰：「高麗去京師四千里，地瘠民貧，夷俗雜尚，非中原比，萬一梗化，疲力治之，非幸事也，不如守祖宗舊制。」
value.en: When the court debated abolishing the Eastern Campaign Secretariat and creating a Three Han province like the others, Yue replied, "Goryeo lies four thousand li from the capital, its land is poor and its customs unlike the Central Plains; if it resisted, pacification would exhaust us—better keep the ancestral arrangement."
value.literal: The court deliberated abolishing the Eastern Campaign Secretariat and establishing a Three Han Secretariat with forms like other provinces; an edict was sent down to the Central Secretariat for mixed discussion; Yue replied: "Goryeo is four thousand li from the capital, its land poor and its people impoverished, its barbarian customs mixed and diverse—not comparable to the Central Plains; if by chance they resisted transformation, to exhaust strength governing them would not be a fortunate affair; better to keep the ancestral old system."

value.zh: 丞相稱善，奏罷議不行。
value.en: The chancellor approved, and the proposal was dropped.
value.literal: The Chancellor praised it and memorialized that the proposal be dropped and not carried out.

value.zh: 高麗人聞之，圖公像歸，祠而事之，曰：「不絕國祀者，王公也。」
value.en: Goryeo people heard of it, brought his portrait home, and worshipped him, saying, "Lord Wang preserved our state's rites."
value.literal: When Goryeo people heard of it they took his portrait home, enshrined and served it, saying: "He who did not cut off our state's sacrifices is Lord Wang."

value.zh: 泰定元年，奉詔廷策天下士，第八剌、張益等八十五人，始增乙科員額至一十五人。
value.en: In Taiding 1 (1324) he conducted the palace examination; Balha, Zhang Yi, and eighty-five others passed, and the second-class quota was raised to fifteen for the first time.
value.literal: In the first year of Taiding he received an edict to conduct palace examinations of scholars empire-wide; Balha, Zhang Yi, and eighty-five others passed; the quota for the second class was for the first time increased to fifteen persons.
